big-news.text: The train drivers' union and Spekter, the employers' group, reached a deal overnight, ending a strike that lasted almost a month. Vy expects most trains to be running normally again from this afternoon.
Norway signed a deal worth billions to send 16.5 tonnes of high-level nuclear waste to Sweden for treatment. It has to come back to Norway by 2055.
A big search is under way in Bodø for a person who went missing after a jet ski capsized overnight. The other rider swam about 200 meters to shore in ice-cold water.

whats-changing.text: If you're driving west, road 52 over Hemsedalsfjellet will close for up to 13.5 hours a day from Oct 21 to Dec 17, though it stays open over weekends. The suggested detours are Rv 7 or E16.

oslo.text: A tram and a taxi collided near Nasjonalmuseet last night. Six people went to the emergency clinic with no serious injuries reported, and tram lines 12 and 15 were delayed.
The city approved only 320 new homes in the first half of the year, against a target of 3,000 a year, which Labour warns will push prices up further.

be-aware.text: There's a small new offshore strike at Reach Subsea, but it won't affect daily life in Oslo.

fun-and-free.text: Top pick: Barnas verdensdager is a free world-culture festival at Grønland today and tomorrow, 11:30–16:30, with music, dance and an international food bazaar.
The Natural History Museum has free dinosaur tours and mini shows at 12:00 on both days.
Art fest at Bærums Verk is free, 12:00–18:00 daily through Wednesday.
Oktoberfest is at Youngstorget today and is back again Oct 22–24.
For a paid night out, Bob Dylan plays Oslo Spektrum and Espen Lind plays Sentrum Scene, both tonight at 20:00.
